title: John Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 12.

questions.question: Who came to Bethany six days before the passover?
questions.explanation: Jesus came to Bethany six days before the passover as stated in John 12:1.

questions.question: What did Mary use to anoint the feet of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Mary took a pound of ointment of spikenard to anoint Jesus' feet according to John 12:3.

questions.question: Who protested about the value of the ointment used by Mary?
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot questioned why the ointment was not sold and given to the poor as mentioned in John 12:4-5.

questions.question: True or False: Lazarus was dead when Jesus arrived in Bethany.
questions.explanation: Lazarus had been dead, but he was raised from the dead by Jesus, indicating he was not dead at the time of Jesus' arrival. (John 12:1)

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the poor?
options: They will always be with you
You should sell everything to help them
questions.correctAnswer: They will always be with you
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that the poor will always be with them, as recorded in John 12:8.

questions.question: True or False: The chief priests wanted to put Lazarus to death.
questions.explanation: The chief priests consulted to put Lazarus to death because many believed on Jesus due to him, as stated in John 12:10-11.

questions.question: What did the people do when they heard Jesus was coming to Jerusalem?
options: They took branches of palm trees
questions.correctAnswer: They took branches of palm trees
questions.explanation: The people took branches of palm trees and went forth to meet Jesus, as described in John 12:13.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples understood what Jesus was doing at first.
questions.explanation: The disciples did not understand these things at first, but later recalled them after Jesus was glorified (John 12:16).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the hour of glorification?
questions.explanation: Jesus indicated that the hour had come for the Son of man to be glorified, as stated in John 12:23.

questions.question: In John 12, which event happens first?
options: Lazarus is raised from the dead
questions.explanation: The first event mentioned is Jesus arriving in Bethany six days before the passover, according to John 12:1.

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen if a corn of wheat does not die?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that unless a corn of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it abideth alone (John 12:24).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus came to judge the world.
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that he did not come to judge the world but to save it (John 12:47).

medium.title: John Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Why did many people come to see Jesus in Bethany?
options: To see Lazarus raised from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: To see Lazarus raised from the dead
questions.explanation: Many people came to see Jesus not only for His sake but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead (John 12:9).

questions.question: What did the chief priests want to do to Lazarus?
questions.explanation: The chief priests consulted to put Lazarus to death because many Jews were believing in Jesus because of Lazarus (John 12:10-11).

questions.question: What did the people shout as they met Jesus on His way to Jerusalem?
options: Blessed is the King of Israel
Glory to God in the highest
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed is the King of Israel
questions.explanation: The people cried out, 'Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord' as they met Jesus (John 12:13).

questions.question: What metaphor does Jesus use to explain the necessity of His death?
questions.explanation: Jesus uses the metaphor of a corn of wheat, explaining that unless it falls to the ground and dies, it remains alone, but if it dies, it brings forth much fruit (John 12:24).

questions.question: What does Jesus say about those who love their life?
options: They will be honored by God
questions.explanation: Jesus states that he who loveth his life shall lose it, indicating a call to self-sacrifice for eternal life (John 12:25).

questions.question: What did Jesus say would happen if He was lifted up from the earth?
options: He would draw all men unto Him
questions.correctAnswer: He would draw all men unto Him
questions.explanation: Jesus indicated that if He were lifted up from the earth, He would draw all men unto Him, referring to His impending crucifixion (John 12:32).

questions.question: Jesus mentions that the prince of this world will be cast out. Who is He referring to?
questions.explanation: When Jesus refers to the prince of this world being cast out, He is speaking about Satan's imminent defeat (John 12:31).

questions.question: How does Jesus describe His mission in John 12:47?
questions.explanation: Jesus states that He came not to judge the world, but to save it, emphasizing His role as the Savior (John 12:47).

questions.question: True or False: The disciples understood everything Jesus said while He was still with them.
questions.explanation: The disciples did not initially understand these things, but later remembered them after Jesus was glorified (John 12:16).

questions.question: True or False: The voice from heaven confirmed Jesus' mission and glorified God's name.
questions.explanation: The voice from heaven declared that God had glorified His name and would glorify it again, affirming Jesus' mission (John 12:28).

questions.question: True or False: Many of the chief rulers believed in Jesus but did not confess Him due to fear of the Pharisees.
questions.explanation: The chief rulers believed on Jesus but did not confess Him for fear of being put out of the synagogue, showing their desire for human praise over God's (John 12:42-43).

questions.question: What does John 12:35 encourage believers to do while they have the light?
options: Walk while you have the light
questions.correctAnswer: Walk while you have the light
questions.explanation: Jesus encourages believers to walk while they have the light, indicating the urgency of faith and following Him before darkness overtakes them (John 12:35).

questions.question: What does Jesus promise to those who serve Him, according to John 12:26?
options: They will be honored by the Father
questions.correctAnswer: They will be honored by the Father
questions.explanation: Jesus promises that whoever serves Him and follows Him will be honored by the Father (John 12:26).

hard.title: John Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 12.

questions.question: What did Mary use to anoint the feet of Jesus?
questions.explanation: Mary took a pound of ointment of spikenard, which was very costly, to anoint the feet of Jesus (John 12:3).

questions.question: Who objected to Mary's act of anointing Jesus and why?
options: Judas Iscariot, because he was a thief
John, because he felt it was inappropriate
Matthew, because he preferred offerings to the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Judas Iscariot, because he was a thief
questions.explanation: Judas Iscariot objected, claiming the ointment could have been sold and the money given to the poor, but he did so out of selfish motives as he was a thief (John 12:4-6).

questions.question: Which significant event happened six days before the Passover?
questions.explanation: Jesus arrived in Bethany six days before the Passover, where Lazarus had been raised from the dead (John 12:1).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the poor in relation to himself?
options: They are more important than me
You will always have the poor with you
They should be prioritized over worship
They will be judged more harshly
questions.correctAnswer: You will always have the poor with you
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that the poor would always be present, but he would not always be with them, emphasizing his imminent departure (John 12:8).

questions.question: What did the people shout when they met Jesus as he came into Jerusalem?
options: Blessed is the King of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Blessed is the King of Israel
questions.explanation: The crowd shouted, 'Blessed is the King of Israel that cometh in the name of the Lord' as they greeted Jesus (John 12:13).

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he referred to a corn of wheat falling into the ground?
options: It refers to the growth of faith
questions.explanation: Jesus used the analogy of a corn of wheat to signify that unless it dies, it remains alone, but if it dies, it brings forth much fruit, foreshadowing his own death and resurrection (John 12:24).

questions.question: According to Jesus, what happens to those who love their life in this world?
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that those who love their life in this world shall lose it, indicating the paradox of self-denial leading to eternal life (John 12:25).

questions.question: What did the voice from heaven affirm when Jesus prayed?
options: I have glorified it, and will glorify it again
questions.correctAnswer: I have glorified it, and will glorify it again
questions.explanation: The voice from heaven responded to Jesus' prayer, affirming that God had glorified His name and would glorify it again (John 12:28).

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he said he came into the world as a light?
options: To show the way to heaven
To save those who believe in him
questions.correctAnswer: To save those who believe in him
questions.explanation: Jesus declared that he came as a light into the world so that whosoever believes on him should not abide in darkness, emphasizing his mission of salvation (John 12:46).

questions.question: According to John 12:43, what did the chief rulers love more than the praise of God?
questions.explanation: The chief rulers loved the praise of men more than the praise of God, which hindered them from confessing their belief in Jesus (John 12:43).

questions.question: True or False: The people who saw Jesus perform miracles believed in him.
questions.explanation: Despite witnessing many miracles, the people did not believe in him, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah (John 12:37).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus came to judge the world.
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that he did not come to judge the world, but to save it, indicating his purpose was one of redemption, not condemnation (John 12:47).

questions.question: What Old Testament prophet is quoted in John 12 regarding belief and revelation?
questions.explanation: The sayings of Esaias (Isaiah) were referenced to explain the unbelief of the people and the fulfillment of prophecy regarding the revelation of God's arm (John 12:38).

questions.question: What is the Greek meaning of the word 'glorify' as used in Jesus' prayer?
questions.explanation: The term 'glorify' in the context of Jesus' prayer means to honor, reflecting the depth of his desire for God's name to be honored through his mission (John 12:28).

questions.question: Which literary device is used in John 12:24 when Jesus speaks about the corn of wheat?
questions.explanation: Jesus uses a metaphor comparing the corn of wheat to his own death, illustrating the principle of sacrifice leading to fruitful results (John 12:24).

theological.title: John Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does John 12:3 reveal about Mary's act of anointing Jesus?
options: It was a costly gift of worship
questions.correctAnswer: It was a costly gift of worship
questions.explanation: John 12:3 states that Mary took a pound of ointment of spikenard, very costly, to anoint Jesus' feet, indicating the great value and significance of her act of worship.

questions.question: In John 12:6, what motive does Judas Iscariot have for questioning Mary's actions?
questions.explanation: John 12:6 clarifies that Judas questioned Mary not out of care for the poor, but because he was a thief and had the bag, indicating his greed.

questions.question: What does Jesus imply about his presence compared to the poor in John 12:8?
options: He will be with them always
His time on earth is limited
questions.correctAnswer: His time on earth is limited
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 12:8, 'For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always,' highlighting the urgency of his ministry before his impending death.

questions.question: What reaction do the chief priests have towards Lazarus in John 12:10?
options: They want to put him to death
questions.correctAnswer: They want to put him to death
questions.explanation: According to John 12:10, the chief priests consulted that they might put Lazarus also to death because many Jews believed in Jesus because of him.

questions.question: How does John 12:19 reflect the Pharisees' concern about Jesus?
options: They felt threatened by his influence
questions.correctAnswer: They felt threatened by his influence
questions.explanation: John 12:19 shows the Pharisees expressing concern by saying, 'Perceive ye how ye prevail nothing? behold, the world is gone after him,' indicating their fear of losing influence.

questions.question: What statement does Jesus make about the necessity of his death in John 12:24?
questions.explanation: In John 12:24, Jesus states that unless a corn of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it abideth alone; but if it dies, it brings forth much fruit, signifying the necessity of his death for salvation.

questions.question: According to John 12:27, what is Jesus' attitude toward his impending death?
questions.explanation: John 12:27 reveals Jesus' turmoil, as he says, 'Now is my soul troubled,' indicating his deep emotional struggle regarding the purpose of his coming hour.

questions.question: What does John 12:32 indicate about the result of Jesus being 'lifted up'?
options: It will draw all men unto him
It will lead to his glory
questions.correctAnswer: It will draw all men unto him
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 12:32, 'And I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me,' referring to the drawing of people to salvation through his crucifixion.

questions.question: What does John 12:36 encourage believers to do while they have light?
questions.explanation: John 12:36 encourages, 'While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light,' urging believers to embrace faith in Jesus while he is present.

questions.question: What does John 12:42 suggest about the faith of the chief rulers?
options: They were fearful of losing status
questions.correctAnswer: They were fearful of losing status
questions.explanation: John 12:42 states that many chief rulers believed on him, but did not confess him for fear of being put out of the synagogue, showing their concern for their social standing.

questions.question: How does John 12:48 describe the consequence of rejecting Jesus' words?
questions.explanation: John 12:48 states that the one who rejects Jesus and does not receive his words has the word that will judge him, highlighting the serious consequence of disbelief.

questions.question: What is the significance of the voice from heaven in John 12:28?
options: It brings confusion among the people
questions.explanation: In John 12:28, the voice from heaven responds to Jesus' prayer, affirming his mission and authority, saying, 'I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.'

questions.question: What doctrine is highlighted in the connection between John 12:25 and John 12:26 regarding discipleship?
questions.explanation: John 12:25 speaks of losing one's life to gain eternal life, while John 12:26 emphasizes serving Jesus involves following him, together teaching that true discipleship requires self-denial.

questions.question: How does John 12:41 contribute to the understanding of Jesus' identity?
options: It indicates he was merely human
It presents him as a teacher only
questions.explanation: John 12:41 indicates that Isaiah spoke of Jesus' glory, enhancing the understanding of Jesus as the divine Messiah who fulfills Old Testament prophecy.

questions.question: What does John 12:34 reveal about the people's misunderstanding of Jesus' mission?
options: They thought he was a prophet
They believed he would conquer Rome
They expected him to live forever
questions.correctAnswer: They expected him to live forever
questions.explanation: John 12:34 captures how the people were confused by Jesus' statement about being lifted up, as they had heard that the Christ abideth forever, reflecting their misunderstanding of his sacrificial mission.
